display.title: Tanya Shiur 27: Chapter 8, Forbidden Foods, Idle Talk and Worldly Wisdom
display.summary_short: Two Yiddish Tanya classes on chapter 8: why forbidden food stays bound to kelipah, how idle and forbidden speech mark the soul, and when secular wisdom may be studied.
display.summary_long: Shiur 27 in Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish Tanya series holds two weekly classes on Tanya chapter 8. The first explains why forbidden foods are called 'issur', bound: even eaten for the sake of Heaven, their life-force cannot be raised to holiness, while permitted food eaten to serve Hashem rises through the words of Torah and prayer. Food eaten only for pleasure leaves a mark on the soul that teshuvah must cleanse. Along the way come a talk on davening as a ladder through the four worlds, the Rebbe teaching a niggun on Simchas Torah, the Alter Rebbe and the over-salted fish, the Frierdiker Rebbe and the spoonful of compote, and a wagon driver asked why he works. The class closes on idle talk: no word is lost, so fill the mouth with Torah and Tehillim. The second class continues the chapter: the Baal Shem Tov's reading of 'ki sir'eh chamor', the Chassidic way of refining the body, stories of Rabbi Nochum of Chernobyl and the Alter Rebbe who could not see what was not holy, guarding thought, zeal from the moment of waking, when the wisdom of the nations may be learned, and a story of a misnaged's blank note before a Rebbe.
display.lesson: What a Jew eats, says and thinks leaves its mark on the soul; using the body and speech for Torah and mitzvos raises them to holiness.

date.note: Shiur 28 is dated 29 Av 5736 in its filename; this class mentions the Rebbe's recent call to repeat the Twelve Pesukim (begun 5736).

study_text.note: Two weekly sessions: start of chapter 8, then middle to end of chapter 8 with a preview of chapter 9.

advisories.note: Discusses the soul's cleansing after death, Gehinnom and the kaf hakela as consequences of forbidden food and speech.

a misnaged who visits a Rebbe
